title: Quiz: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids

questions.stem: What are the products when a reactive metal reacts with water?
questions.explanation: When a reactive metal reacts with water, it produces a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas. For example: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂.

questions.stem: What are the products when a metal reacts with a dilute acid?
questions.explanation: When a metal reacts with a dilute acid, it produces a salt and hydrogen gas. For example: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. The type of salt depends on the acid used.

questions.stem: Which observation would you expect when potassium is added to water?

options.text: It fizzes gently and slowly dissolves
It floats, moves around rapidly, and may catch fire with a lilac flame

questions.explanation: Potassium is very reactive. It floats on water (it is less dense), moves rapidly on the surface, produces hydrogen gas which may ignite with a lilac flame, and the potassium melts into a ball from the heat produced.

questions.stem: Which metal does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series and therefore does not react with dilute acids. Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from acids.

questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for magnesium reacting with dilute sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Mg + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂ is the balanced equation. One magnesium atom reacts with one molecule of sulfuric acid to produce magnesium sulfate and one molecule of hydrogen gas.

questions.stem: How can you test for hydrogen gas produced in these reactions?

options.text: It makes a squeaky pop with a burning splint
It turns damp litmus paper red

questions.explanation: Hydrogen gas is tested by holding a burning splint near the mouth of the test tube. If hydrogen is present, it burns with a squeaky pop sound.

questions.stem: Why does calcium react with water but iron does not?

options.text: Calcium is a larger atom than iron
Calcium is more reactive than iron and loses its outer electrons more easily
Iron does not contain any electrons to lose

questions.explanation: Calcium is higher in the reactivity series than iron. It loses its outer electrons more easily to form Ca²⁺ ions, so it reacts with cold water. Iron is less reactive and can only react with steam, not cold water.
